messages:
maria: heads-up — I hit a flakiness spike in the OTLP exporter during a cross-region failover. gRPC streams were dying after ~30s with connect resets.

dennis: same region? any pattern on message size or concurrency?

maria: mostly chat spans, nothing huge. concurrency spiked when the canary rollout started. noticed a ton of HTTP/2 GOAWAYs.

olivia: GOAWAYs often point to max_concurrent_streams exhaustion or the backend closing idle connections. which exporter config are you using?

maria: default grpc exporter: 
```yaml
exporter: otlp_grpc
endpoint: otlp.redwood.internal:4317
timeout: 10s
retry: on
```
but we rely on SDK defaults for dial/connect timeouts.

sam: SDKs usually have two places to set deadlines: dial/connect and per-RPC. If dial timeout is too long, you can end up with many pending connections during load bumps which exhaust file descriptors.

jin: also watch keepalive and TCP TIME_WAIT behavior — idle timeouts from our egress proxy were 30s, which matches your window. proxy could be closing streams aggressively.

maria: ah that fits. proxy has 30s idle, and backend sets max_concurrent_streams=100. Our per-process batcher opens ~120 simultaneous streams during bursts.

dennis: proposal: make exporter default dial timeout 3s, per-RPC deadline 8s, and add jittered exponential backoff with max elapsed 60s. plus a client-side retry admission control to avoid thundering herd.

olivia: love the retry admission idea — basically a local token bucket that gates retries? we should skimp retries for large payloads or idempotency=false.

sam: exactly. suggest config knobs: "retry_admission_capacity", "max_retry_attempts", "retry_backoff_base_ms", "retry_backoff_max_ms", and an "admission_per_host" toggle so we don't overflow one backend.

maria: can we also add a dialer-level deadline skew? i.e. ensure dial deadline < per-rpc deadline by margin so we don't hit per-rpc timeout mid-handshake. saw TLS handshake lasting 2.5s occasionally.

jin: yes — dial_deadline = rpc_deadline - dial_margin. default dial_margin 2s. this avoids ambiguous failures.

olivia: UX question: do we expose all these knobs in the console routes screen (per-service exporter config) or keep as advanced YAML only? product wants minimal surface.

dennis: default safe values in console, advanced link for YAML. show a warning if you set per-rpc < dial_margin. also surface observed GOAWAY/connection-reset counts in telemetry so users can reason about it.

maria: +1. For ops, we should emit exporter-internal spans/events: dial_start, dial_success/fail, rpc_attempt, backoff_ms, admitted_retry/denied_retry. correlate to span IDs.

ci-bot: test-run queued: exporter-integration/dialer-deadline-tests ✓

sam: one more: add a soft retry budget shared across all exporters per host to avoid cross-tenant amplification. like 100 retries/sec per host, burstable.

jin: implementable in SDK with token bucket that refills at host-level. we can expose telemetry counters: retry_denied_due_to_budget.

maria: timeline? i can drive a PR for SDK defaults + console flags. plan: SDK PR with tests, integration harness to repro proxy idle cut, and console PR to surface basic knobs + warnings.

dennis: ping me on the PR, i'll wire telemetry alert rule for GOAWAY > 0.1% of requests in a minute.

olivia: also add a runbook note: if you see GOAWAY spikes, check proxy idle timeout, TLS handshake latency, and max_concurrent_streams.

maria: thanks — opening PRs today. will post small repro and test data here when ready.

sam: thanks all — sounds solid. :thumbsup:
